Black-box tests of a Warp SQL server: they speak the protocol over HTTP with
[`warp.py`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/conformance/tests/warp.py), a few plain calls with nothing hidden, so a failure points at
the protocol rather than at a driver. The suite fails, never skips, when it has no server
to talk to.

```bash
uv venv .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -e .
WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_BINARY=../cpp/build/warp-duckdb .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
```

## Pointing it at a server

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_BINARY` | | A server binary to start (taking `--host`, `--port`) |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_PASSWORD_ENV` | `WARP_DUCKDB_PASSWORD` | The variable it reads its administrator's password from |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_USERNAME` | `warp` | That administrator's name |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_LOG` | a temporary file | Where the started server's output goes |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_URL`, `WARP_SQL_TEST_USERNAME`, `WARP_SQL_TEST_PASSWORD` | | A running server instead (then deselect `-m "not mtls and not own_server"`) |

Tests marked `mtls` and `own_server` start servers of their own, with flags that differ
between servers; the defaults are `warp-duckdb`'s:

| Variable | Default | Hardcharger's |
|---|---|---|
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_MTLS_FLAG` | `--tls-client-ca` | `--mtls-ca-cert` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_CORS_FLAG` | `--cors-origin` | `--cors-origins` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_IDLE_FLAG` | `--session-idle-timeout-seconds` | `--session-idle-timeout` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_TOKEN_LIFETIME_FLAG` | `--token-lifetime-seconds` | |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_DRAIN_FLAG` | `--drain-seconds` | `--shutdown-grace-period-seconds` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_HEALTH_QUERY_FLAG` | `--health-check-query` | `--health-check-query` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_RETENTION_FLAG` | `--result-retention-seconds` | `--result-retention-seconds` |
| `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_OAUTH_ARGS`, `WARP_SQL_TEST_SERVER_OAUTH_SECRET_ENV` | see [`test_oauth_browser.py`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/conformance/tests/test_oauth_browser.py) | see there |

[`test_authorization.py`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/conformance/tests/test_authorization.py) needs a server with SQL privileges
and the `WARP_SQL_TEST_AUTHZ_*` variables its docstring describes; on a server without
privileges (`warp-duckdb`) it skips, saying so.

## Every response against the OpenAPI document

[`openapi_check.py`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/conformance/tests/openapi_check.py) holds every response the suite receives to
[`spec/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/spec/openapi.yaml): `conftest.py` wraps `httpx.Client.send`, so each
request of every test (fixtures included) is checked, and a response that disagrees fails
the test that made it, saying what was wrong. For each response it finds the operation by
method and path and checks:

- the status is documented for the operation (exactly, or by its `4XX`/`5XX` range);
- the content type is one the response documents;
- the required headers are there, and every documented header's value fits its schema;
- a JSON body validates against the response's schema (JSON Schema 2020-12, which OpenAPI
  3.1 schemas are), and a problem document's `status` and `type` agree with the response;
- an Arrow body begins like an Arrow IPC stream (the tests read the rest);
- a path or method outside the document gets a `404` or `405` problem document.

The end of a run says how many of the document's operations had responses checked (all 38
against `warp-duckdb`). [`test_openapi.py`](https://github.com/gizmodata/warp-sql/blob/main/conformance/tests/test_openapi.py) also checks that the
document is valid OpenAPI 3.1, that it and the spec's Appendix B list the same 38 endpoints
(and that every endpoint a section names is in Appendix B), which endpoints need no token,
the served document (`GET /warp/v1/openapi.json`, spec [§3.3](/specification/#33-get-warpv1openapijson-optional-capability-openapi): unauthenticated, cacheable, the
published document apart from `servers` and `x-` fields), and that the check itself rejects
a real response broken on purpose (a renamed or missing field, an unknown enumeration value,
an undocumented status, content type or missing header, a problem document that disagrees
with its status).

`WARP_SQL_TEST_OPENAPI` names another copy of the document to check against. A test that
must see a response the document doesn't describe takes `@pytest.mark.openapi_unchecked`
(none does).

## MUSTs without a test

Every MUST of the spec that a server can be tested for has a test, except these:

| Spec | MUST | Why not yet |
|---|---|---|
| [§2.1](/specification/#21-transport) | Every operation works over HTTP/1.1 through an ordinary reverse proxy | Needs a proxy in the harness |
| [§2.3](/specification/#23-identifiers) | Ids carry at least 128 bits of randomness | A black box can't measure entropy: `test_ids_are_long_random_strings` refuses ids too short or regular to hold it, no more |
| [§2.6](/specification/#26-response-headers-defined-by-this-protocol) | `Retry-After` is delta-seconds on `429` | Tested on `503` (draining); no portable way to make a server rate-limit |
| [§4.4](/specification/#44-client-certificate-sign-in-optional-capability-mtls_identity) | An identity shown in error details or logs is escaped | Refusing such identities is tested; their escaping in a server's logs is not visible to the suite |
| [§4.4](/specification/#44-client-certificate-sign-in-optional-capability-mtls_identity) | Tokens a principal derives from a bound token keep the binding | The protocol has no way to derive one (an engine's scoped tokens are its own SQL); Hardcharger tests its own (`test_mtls_identity.py`) |
| [§9.3](/specification/#93-results-are-governed-data) | Retained results stored outside memory are protected like the source data and deleted on expiry or session end | Storage is outside the protocol |
| [§9.5](/specification/#95-browsers) | `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response | Checked on a sample of responses, not all |
| [§9.6](/specification/#96-client-certificates) | No TLS 1.2 renegotiation to change the certificate | Python's `ssl` can't start a renegotiation |

These MUSTs bind clients, not servers, so a server suite can't test them: [§3.1](/specification/#31-get-warp) (use only
listed features), [§4.1](/specification/#41-post-warpv1authtoken) (tokens are opaque), [§5.6](/specification/#56-sessions-that-no-longer-exist) (a new token after `session_ended` for the
token reasons), [§6.1](/specification/#61-submit-post-warpv1sessionssession_idstatements) (check `Content-Type`), [§6.2](/specification/#62-the-statement-document) (a `failed` or `cancelled` document is an
error), [§6.6](/specification/#66-errors-during-a-result-stream) (an incomplete stream is a failed result), [§6.10](/specification/#610-partitioned-results) (read every partition to its
end, all at once, and never guess a missing `Warp-Result-Order`), [§8.2](/specification/#82-compression) (read buffers left
uncompressed), [§8.3](/specification/#83-partitioned-ingest) (no reliance on row order after a partitioned ingest) and [§12](/specification/#12-versioning) (ignore
what is unknown, accept unknown enumeration values). The drivers' own suites test them.

[§2.1](/specification/#21-transport)'s "say so in its documentation" (a base path other than `/warp`) and [§4.4](/specification/#44-client-certificate-sign-in-optional-capability-mtls_identity)'s "end TLS
at the server" are about documentation and deployment.
